ceviri.65: From Script to Storyboard: The Pre-Production Stages
ceviri.66: A commercial film begins with a script written by TasarımMania's copywriters in line with the brand brief.
ceviri.67: The draft goes to the client for sign-off scene by scene; every revision is put on record in writing, which keeps the process clear. Once the script is approved it moves on to the storyboard stage. The storyboard is a checking layer that tests camera angles, scene transitions and timing against visual sketches before the shoot; when that stage is skipped, uncertainty on the shooting day and the risk of a reshoot both rise. Once the character design and the scene composition are settled, the team goes on location with a route map already in hand.
ceviri.69: Animation or Live Action? The Format Decision
ceviri.70: A live-action commercial rests on physical production elements: the cast, the location and the lighting setup. Once the storyboard is approved, the shooting plan and the location arrangements come into play.
ceviri.71: An animated commercial, by contrast, rests on scene design, character animation and background illustration produced digitally. Both formats go through the same script-and-storyboard logic, but the production method differs at the root: brands aiming at abstract ideas or character-led storytelling usually go for animation, while stories that need a real location and a human subject favour the live-action format. In both formats the voiceover is recorded in a studio with professional voice artists and synchronised to the picture in the final mix. The claim the film makes is scrutinised too;

ceviri.77: On the left, a document with a folded corner and three text bars on it; beneath it the words “Brand brief”. An arrow runs from it to the right. On the right, a longer document: three short bold bars stand for the scene headings, and the thin bars below them for the dialogue lines; beneath it the word “Script”. ceviri.82: Storyboard: composition sketches in six frames, one of them approved — illustrative graphic
ceviri.83: At the top, the heading “Camera angles” and the label “visual sketch”. Below it, six square frames in two rows: one a wide shot with a horizontal horizon line, one a close-up with a circle in the centre, one a product shown as a small rectangle, and bar compositions in the remaining three. Under the frames there is a thin bar in place of a sequence number. The middle frame in the second row has an accent border and a tick, with “Approved” beneath it. At the very bottom, a single line: “The shooting plan comes after storyboard sign-off”. There is no face and no real footage in the frames.
ceviri.87: The shooting plan comes after storyboard sign-off
ceviri.89: Format decision: the Animation and Live action cards side by side, weighted equally — illustrative graphic
ceviri.90: Two equal cards side by side. On the left, “Animation”: a stack of three rectangles offset over one another, with a small timeline beneath it. On the right, “Live action”: three badges — Cast, Location and Lighting — each made of an icon and a label. The two cards are the same size, with the same border and fill; neither is dimmed or crossed out. At the very bottom, a single line: “Chosen to suit the need”.
ceviri.101: It draws the pre-production route the page describes: from the brand brief to the script, then on to storyboard sign-off and the format decision. The documents and frames are an example drawing, not taken from a real project; scene names, lines of dialogue and frame numbers are all represented by bars so as not to invent them, and there are no faces in the frames. The two cards at the third stop are equal on purpose: the page presents animation and live action as two valid options, and which one gets used is decided by the need. The timeline is there only to say “timing is being planned”; it shows no duration, budget or frame count, which is why there is deliberately no number anywhere in the graphic.

_kararlar.reklam filmi → commercial film: Blog başlığı çevirisiyle tutarlı (en-blog-ceviri-uret.js). 'advert film' Britanya'da konuşma dili, sayfa başlığında zayıf kalıyor.
_kararlar.çekimli → live action: Animasyonun karşıtı olarak sektörün terimi. 'shot format' anlaşılmazdı.
_kararlar.seslendirme → voiceover · seslendirme sa: İkisi de Britanya prodüksiyon terimi; 'voice-over artist' de doğru ama iki kelime yeterli.
_kararlar.renk düzeltmesi → colour grade: Sözlükteki 'renk düzenleme → colour grading, correction DEĞİL' kararının aynısı. Türkçe metinde 'düzeltme' geçse de kastedilen final bakış katmanı; sitenin tek İngilizcesi olsun diye 'grade'.
_kararlar.mecra → channel: Televizyon/dijital/sosyal ayrımı yapılan yerlerde 'channel'; 'medium' fazla soyut kalıyordu.
_kararlar.oyuncu → cast · oyuncu hakları → perform: Sözlükteki 'telif ücreti (oyuncu) → performers' fees' kararıyla aynı aile. 'Actor rights' hukuki olarak yanlış çağrışım yapıyor.
_kararlar.72 ticari reklam kuralları: Bağlantı ticaret.gov.tr'ye gidiyor; /sosyal-medya/ sayfasındaki çeviriyle birebir aynı tutuldu.
_kararlar.63 '0 format' → '0 formats': data-birim=" format" özniteliğini en-birim.js bu yedek metinden türetiyor; çoğul yazılmazsa sayaç 'formats' değil 'format' der.
_kararlar.69 soru işareti: H2 Türkçede soru biçiminde ('Animasyon mu, Çekimli mi?'). Denetim hizmet sayfalarında soru biçimli H2 arıyor — soru işareti korundu.
